'''Diana E. Northup''' is an American microbiologist, speleologist, ecologist, Visiting Professor of Biology, and Professor Emerita of Library Sciences with the [[University of New Mexico]]. Her research focuses on the microbial ecology of caves around the world. Dr. Northup is a Fellow of the [[National Speleological Society]] and the [[Cave Research Foundation]]. She wrote the [[Wiley (publisher)|Wiley]] textbook ''Microbial Ecology''.<ref name=":2">{{Cite book |last=Barton |first=Larry |title=Microbial ecology |date=2011 |publisher=Wiley-Blackwell |others=Diana E. Northup |isbn=978-1-118-01582-7 |location=Hoboken, N.J. |oclc=757394257}}</ref> She was awarded the [[National Speleological Society]] Science Prize in 2013.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=NSS Science Awardees|url=https://caves.org/committee/award?scienceAwardees.shtml|access-date=2021-07-09|website=caves.org|language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Northup was an undergraduate student at [[West Virginia University]], where she studied political science. She moved to the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]] for graduate studies, where she earned a Master's of Library Science in 1972. Northup moved to the [[University of New Mexico]], where she earned a Master's degree in biology in 1988. She remained at the University of New Mexico for her doctoral research, where she studied the geomicrobiology of caves.<ref name=":3">{{Cite thesis|title=Geomicrobiology of caves|date=2002|language=English|first=Diana E|last=Northup|oclc=51209753}}</ref>{{Page needed|date=November 2021}}

== Research and career ==
Northup is a visiting associate professor at the [[University of New Mexico]] where she started the Subsurface Life In Mineral Environments (SLIME) team.<ref>{{Cite web|title=SLIME Team People|url=https://www.caveslime.org/people/|access-date=2021-07-09|website=www.caveslime.org}}</ref> In particular, Northup studies the colorful ferromanganese deposits that line the walls of [[Lechuguilla Cave|Lechuguilla]] and [https://www.nps.gov/media/photo/gallery-item.htm?id=00BDA79B-155D-451F-6737D552DE9FFADC&gid=002834EA-155D-451F-6776BADA00BE0B71 Spider Cave] in Carlsbad Caverns National Park.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=The Explorers Club -|url=https://explorers.org/events/detail/chapter_event_southwest5|access-date=2021-07-09|website=explorers.org}}</ref> Her work on the [[Lechuguilla Cave]] was featured in a [[PBS]] [[Nova (American TV program)|Nova]] episode, "The Mysterious Life of Caves."<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Diana Northup on Nova|url=https://biology.unm.edu/biologynews/DNorthupNova.htm|access-date=2021-07-09|website=biology.unm.edu}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=NOVA {{!}} Mysterious Life of Caves {{!}} The Lives of Extremophiles |url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/nova/caves/extremophiles.html |access-date=2024-10-01 |website=www.pbs.org}}</ref> She is also interested in the hydrogen sulfide cave  known as'Cueva de las Sardinas' or 'Cueva de Villa Luz' in [[Tabasco]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Diana Northup|url=http://extraordinarywls.blogspot.com/2015/01/diana-northup.html|access-date=2021-07-09|website=extraordinarywls.blogspot.com|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":4" />

Northup was elected Fellow of the [[National Speleological Society]] in 1992,<ref>{{Cite web |title=NSS Fellows Awardees |url=https://caves.org/committee/award/ |access-date=2021-07-09 |website=caves.org |language=en}}</ref> awarded their Science Prize in 2013,<ref name=":0" /> and presented a Luminary talk in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 Luminary Series - Diana Northup |url=https://caves.org/webinars/2015-luminary-series-diana-northup/ |access-date=2024-10-01 |website=National Speleological Society |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2011, Northup gave a TEDx talk about how she got started in caving and how that influences her mentoring of students.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XuIYzZcvW7w |title=TEDxABQ - Dr. Diana Northup - Using your Passion to Mentor |date=2011-10-26 |last=TEDx Talks |access-date=2024-10-01 |via=YouTube}}</ref>
